source_name: IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Business (IRDAI/HLT/CIR/PRO/84/5/2024, 29 May 2024); IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulations 2024; IRDAI Guidelines on Standardization of Exclusions
notes: Regulatory defaults used until a client supplies its own policy wording. Values marked 'typical' are common market terms, not regulatory limits: replace them with the client's product terms.

terms.description: No claims in the first 30 days of the first policy, except accidents (standard exclusion Excl03).
Pre-existing diseases are covered after continuous cover of at most 36 months.
Named diseases/procedures (e.g. cataract, hernia, joint replacement) have a waiting period. 24 months is typical; the regulatory maximum is 36.
terms.source: IRDAI standard exclusions, Excl02; Master Circular 2024

terms.description: After 60 continuous months of cover, a claim cannot be contested for non-disclosure or misrepresentation, except proven fraud.
Hospitalisation means admission for at least 24 consecutive in-patient care hours, except listed day care procedures.
Medical expenses incurred up to 30 days before admission (typical product term).
Medical expenses incurred up to 60 days after discharge (typical product term).
Room rent capped at 1% of sum insured per day (ICU 2%). Typical capped-product term; many products have no cap.
If a costlier room than eligible is taken, associated expenses are reduced in proportion, but never pharmacy, consumables, implants, medical devices or diagnostics, and not for ICU charges.
Decision on a cashless authorisation request within 1 hour.
Final cashless authorisation within 3 hours of the discharge request.
Reimbursement claims settled or rejected within 30 days of the last necessary document.
In-patient AYUSH treatment is covered up to the sum insured.

codes.Excl05: Rest cure, rehabilitation and respite care
codes.Excl13: Treatments at health hydros, nature cure clinics, spas
codes.Excl14: Dietary supplements and substances bought without prescription

terms.description: IRDAI standardised exclusion codes. Products may cover some (e.g. maternity) by explicit benefit.
terms.source: IRDAI Guidelines on Standardization of Exclusions in Health Insurance Contracts
